class.name: WorldFire
class.brief_description: The fire contract: where fire burns and has burnt, as the other world systems read it.
class.description: Answers for every live fire producer at once ([code]PhysXFireSpread3D[/code]): the most heat and the most burnt of any of them at a point. With none, both are 0. The weather dries the surface water under a fire from [method heat_at]. Get it from [WorldContracts]; a test extends it in a script and sets it with [method WorldContracts.set_fire].

method.name: burn_changed
method.description: Reports that [method burn_age_at] changed over [param area] (x, z in metres): a burn scar placed, moved or aged, or ground a live fire burnt. Readers that cache the ages (grass regrowth) sample them again there and rebuild only what stands on it. Report as the ground burns, at most a few times a second, with the union of the cells in between.

method.name: get_burn_changes_since
method.description: The areas reported by [method burn_changed] after [param generation], merged: [code]{"complete": bool, "area": Rect2}[/code]. [code]complete[/code] is [code]false[/code] when the log (the last 64 reports) no longer reaches back that far: read every age again. An empty [code]area[/code] with [code]complete[/code] true: nothing changed.

method.name: get_burn_generation
method.description: How many [method burn_changed] reports there have been. A reader keeps the generation it last read at and compares.

method.name: burn_age_at
method.description: Years of game time since the ground at [param position] last burnt, for the vegetation's regrowth: the most recent of any producer, a fire in play or an authored [WorldBurnScar3D]. [code]-1[/code] where it never burnt.

method.name: burnt_at
method.description: How burnt the ground at [param position] is, 0 unburnt to 1 burnt out.

method.name: crown_scorch_at
method.description: How high the fire killed tree crowns over [param position], in metres: the lethal scorch height of the front that passed (Van Wagner 1973), or 1000 where a crown burnt. [TreeWind3D] takes the share of a crown below it, with its bark, for whether the tree died (Ryan and Reinhardt 1988); a dead tree stands as a snag that weakens over the years ([method burn_age_at]). The most of any fire; 0 where none burnt.

method.name: has_provider
method.description: Whether any fire producer is live.

method.name: heat_at
method.description: The fire's heat release over the ground at [param position] now, in W/m2; 0 where nothing burns.

method.name: plumes
method.description: Every fire's convection column: x, y and z of where its plume rises from and w its convective heat, W. [WeatherMap3D] lifts each through the air and, where it passes the condensation level, makes a fire cloud over it (pyrocumulus; a pyrocumulonimbus from the largest fires). Empty where nothing flames.

method.name: smoke_sources
method.description: Every fire's smoke: x, y and z of where it rises from and w its particulate (PM2.5) in kg per second of the fire's own (real) time. [WeatherMap3D] carries it as a smoke layer that hazes the air and dims and reddens the sun.

method.name: stem_char_at
method.description: How deep a stem standing at [param position] has charred at its foot, in metres of bark and wood: the time flames and smouldering logs stood there, at a charring rate of about 0.8 mm a minute (EN 1995-1-2). [TreeWind3D] weakens the stem's foot by it, so a burnt tree may snap there in a later storm. The most of any fire; 0 where none burnt.

method.name: water_repellency_at
method.description: How water-repellent the fire left the soil at [param position], 0 to 1: heated soil takes a waxy coat from the burning litter (DeBano 2000; Doerr et al. 2000), so rain runs off a fresh burn scar instead of soaking in. [GroundSurface3D] cuts its infiltration by up to nine tenths by it, so the runoff and its rills come sooner. Fades over a year or two of the weather's clock. The most of any fire; 0 where none burnt.

method.name: wind_at
method.description: The wind the fires draw in near the ground at [param position], in m/s (horizontal): the indraft at the base of their plumes, toward the burning front, strongest within a few metres of it. Summed over the fires; it adds to [method WorldWeather.wind_at]. Zero where no fire is near.
